_comment: Recomp workout file. `_structure` describes every field — hand this whole file to an assistant, ask it to rewrite `program`, then import the result back into the app.

_structure.//: This block IS the documentation. Edit `program`, `settings`, `customExercises` or `history`, keep `_format`, and import the file back into the app.
_structure._format: string — "recomp-workout/v2". Files written by v1 still import; their sets are upgraded automatically.

settings.name: string — who the app greets
settings.queueIndex: integer — which entry of program.days comes next; it wraps around
settings.sound: boolean, optional (v2) — ring a bell when the rest timer runs out
settings.bars: object, optional (v2) — { kg: { olympic, ez, smith, fixed }, lb: {…} }. What an empty bar weighs at your gym. Omitted keys fall back to 20/10/15/15 kg and 45/25/35/35 lb.

program.name: string — shown as the kicker on the home screen
program.days: array, walked in order and then repeated from the top
program.days[].focus: string — e.g. "Full Body #1", "Push", "Rest". Any focus containing the word "rest" renders as a rest day
program.days[].block: string, optional — training block this day belongs to
program.days[].week: integer, optional — week number within the programme
program.days[].exercises: array — leave it empty ([]) on rest days
program.days[].exercises[].exerciseId: string — an id from _reference.exercises, or one you define in customExercises
program.days[].exercises[].repMin: integer 1-100 — bottom of the target rep range
program.days[].exercises[].repMax: integer 1-100 — top of the range; set equal to repMin for an exact target
program.days[].exercises[].rpe: number 5-10, optional — target effort for the set
program.days[].exercises[].rest: string, optional — rest in minutes, e.g. "2-3"
program.days[].exercises[].note: string, optional — a coaching note shown under the exercise name

_structure.customExercises: array, optional — [{ id, name, muscle, equipment, type: "compound" | "isolation", cues: [string], load }]. Use this to add movements the built-in library does not have.
_structure.customExercises[].load: object, optional (v2) — { mode, bar }. mode is "bar" (you enter plates per side, the app doubles them and adds the bar), "dbPair" (you enter one dumbbell, it is doubled), "dbOne" (single-arm, one dumbbell is the whole load), "stack" (machine or cable, read straight off the pin) or "body" (bodyweight, blank counts as 0). bar is "olympic" | "ez" | "smith" | "fixed" and only applies to mode "bar". Leave `load` out and it is inferred from `equipment`.
_structure.history: array of finished sessions, oldest first. Safe to leave untouched.

history[].id: number — unique, used to de-duplicate on merge
history[].focus: string — the day's focus at the time
history[].partial: boolean, optional — true when the session was ended early
history[].entries: [{ exerciseId: string, sets: [{ weight: string, reps: string, entry: string }] }]
history[].entries[].sets[].weight: total load moved, in settings.units. "0" means bodyweight.
history[].entries[].sets[].entry: string, optional (v2) — what was actually loaded: plates on one side, or one dumbbell. Absent on v1 files, where it is worked back out of `weight`.
